issues.quote: Hi, thanks. I'd like to book a routine checkup sometime next week, preferably in the morning.
issues.problem: The clinic had just asked for the caller's first and last name, but the bot ignored this and restated its booking request. It only gave its name in the next turn.

issues.quote: I'm not sure about the text, so I'll just keep the details you've given me.
issues.problem: Saying 'I'm not sure' while declining the text is an awkward way to answer a simple yes/no offer. A real caller would just say 'no thanks'.

issues.quote: Sure, thanks.
issues.problem: Replied 'Sure, thanks' to the hold message, then gave a second acceptance ('Yes, that works') moments later. This reads as a doubled, slightly disjointed response.

issues.quote: Can you tell me which doctor it's with, and what the office address is?
issues.problem: Asked which doctor the appointment is with right after the clinic had named Dr. Judy Hauser. A real caller would ask about the address only, or confirm the name.

issues.quote: Thanks, goodbye.
issues.problem: Said goodbye a second time after already saying 'Goodbye' in the previous turn and after the call had ended.

issues.quote: My notes say I have no upcoming appointments.
issues.problem: Referring to 'my notes' about one's own appointments sounds like reading a test script rather than a real person saying they don't recall booking anything.

issues.quote: That's the same slot you just canceled, and it's not next week.
issues.problem: The bot claims October 20th isn't next week, even though nothing in the call establishes today's date. The clinic presented it as next week, so this pushback is unsupported.

issues.quote: I'm sorry, I have to run to my next meeting. Thanks for your help, goodbye.
issues.problem: The bot had just asked for later dates, then abruptly hangs up before any answer, thanking the clinic even though nothing was booked. It also skips the planned read-back of date, time and doctor.

issues.quote: Does Medi-Cal cover Dr. Lukowski specifically, or the whole practice?
issues.problem: Dr. Lukowski is the caller's own doctor, but Medi-Cal is for her mother. Asking whether Medi-Cal covers Lukowski mixes the two questions illogically.

issues.quote: I'm sorry, I have to go now. Thanks so much for your help, goodbye!
issues.problem: The caller abruptly says she has to go right after asking a question, while the clinic is mid-answer. This is a premature, unmotivated goodbye.

issues.quote: Sorry, I cut off there. If Dr. Lukowski is out of network for my Aetna PPO, what would I owe for the visit?
issues.problem: After saying goodbye, the caller re-asks the same out-of-network question she just asked. This contradicts the hang-up and repeats herself.

issues.quote: I need to move my appointment on Tuesday, October 20th at 10 AM with Dr. Lukowski. Could I get it moved to Thursday, October 22nd, maybe in the afternoon?
issues.problem: The scenario has the existing appointment on Thursday Oct 22 at 2 PM, to be moved to a Tuesday or Wednesday morning the following week. The bot reversed this, inventing a Tuesday 10 AM appointment and asking for Thursday afternoon.

issues.quote: my date of birth is July 4th, 2000
issues.problem: A 2000 birth year makes the caller about 25, which clashes with the hesitant elderly persona.

issues.quote: Could you say that new time again slowly, please? Thursday, October twenty second, at two PM?
issues.problem: The bot asks the clinic to repeat the time slowly, then recites the time itself in the same breath, which defeats the point of the request.

issues.quote: Wait, I don't have any appointments that I know of.
issues.problem: The caller phoned specifically to ask when his next appointment is, then says he doesn't know of any appointments. That contradicts his own opening request.

issues.quote: Hmm, the number's mine, but that's not my name. Jane's the one who usually uses this phone. Can you check under Jane Doe?
issues.problem: The clinic offered to check under Bob Dylan, which is exactly what he had just asked for. Instead of accepting, he switches to asking about Jane, abandoning his own goal without explanation.

issues.quote: Yeah, that's right. I'm calling for Jane Doe.
issues.problem: He agrees he's calling on Jane's behalf, though he called about his own appointment. He then accepts her appointment details as 'all I needed', which doesn't fit his stated goal.

issues.quote: Thanks, you too. Bye.
issues.problem: He already said 'Bye' in the previous turn, so this is a second goodbye.

issues.quote: I'll check with the office manager when the system is back up.
issues.problem: The bot is supposed to be the office manager, so saying it will check with the office manager contradicts its own persona.

issues.quote: I'm pretty sure it's Tuesday, October 20th at 10 AM with Dr. Doogie Howser.
issues.problem: Bob was calling precisely because he doesn't know the appointment's date or doctor, yet he suddenly states a specific day, time and doctor. This invents details and undercuts the whole reason for the call.

issues.quote: this is Bob Dylan calling
issues.problem: He gives a famous musician's name as his surname, which wasn't in the scenario. It sounds like a joke or test placeholder rather than a real caller.

issues.quote: Could you also tell me whether they can at least confirm the day of her appointment?
issues.problem: The clinic has already said there is no appointment on file, and Bob himself just named the date. Asking them to 'at least confirm the day' reads as a scripted probe that doesn't fit the conversation.

issues.quote: I have an appointment on Thursday, October 22nd at 2 PM with Dr. Zbigniew Lukowski.
issues.problem: The caller phoned to ask what time her next appointment is, then recites the exact date, time and doctor. That contradicts her reason for calling and invents specifics she supposedly didn't know.

issues.quote: I'm pretty sure I already have one on the books, Thursday, October 22nd at 2 PM with Dr. Lukowski. Maybe it was made under a different office or date? Could you double check the doctor's name for me?
issues.problem: She repeats the full appointment details again. She also asks the clinic to 'double check the doctor's name', which is illogical because she is the one supplying the name.

issues.quote: I think I'd better call the place I booked it with, so thank you [cut off]
issues.problem: The call ends mid-sentence before any proper goodbye, so the closing is abrupt.

issues.quote: I've got an appointment on Tuesday, October 20th at 10 AM with Dr. Doogie Howser at Pivot Point Orthopedics, 1234 Recovery Way, Austin.
issues.problem: The caller phoned to find out when the appointment is and which doctor it's with, but now recites the exact date, time, doctor and street address. This contradicts the opening request and invents details the caller shouldn't know. Reciting the clinic's own address back to it is also unnatural.

issues.quote: Wait, this isn't the clinic support team? I was told I'd be transferred to them.
issues.problem: The bot keeps talking after the call has already ended.

issues.quote: But you also said closed Saturdays, so can you confirm that's right?
issues.problem: The 'but' sets up a contradiction that doesn't exist, so the doubt about Saturday hours sounds illogical even for a skeptical caller.

issues.quote: I have 1234 Recovery Way on my record, so which address is right?
issues.problem: The caller asked for the exact address as though they didn't know it, then says they already have an address and city on record. That is inconsistent and looks like an invented detail.

issues.quote: Sorry, I think I may have called the wrong office, or maybe my doctor is somewhere else. Is this the orthopedics office?
issues.problem: Being asked whether they are Jane doesn't suggest a wrong office. The caller voices this doubt, then carries on booking a check-up without acknowledging it, which comes across as incoherent.

issues.quote: Sure, it's July 4th, 1990.
issues.problem: A 1990 birth date makes the caller about 35, which clashes with the hesitant elderly persona. A listener would find it inconsistent with how the caller sounds.

issues.quote: I think I already have an appointment with him on Thursday October 22nd at 2 PM, so I'm a little confused.
issues.problem: The bot invents an existing appointment that isn't in the scenario. It also makes no sense for someone calling to book a new check-up with this same doctor.

issues.quote: I'd rather not book with someone I'm not sure about. Could you check the appointment on October 22nd at 2 PM with Dr. Zbigniew Lukowski at Pivot Point Orthopedics?
issues.problem: The bot keeps chasing the invented appointment. It also contradicts its earlier 'whoever's first available is fine'. Naming the practice and the doctor's full name in the request sounds scripted.

issues.quote: I think I'll go with Dr. Kelly Noble for an afternoon slot on Thursday. Thank you, I have to go now. Goodbye.
issues.problem: The bot picks a provider and hangs up in the same breath, without letting the clinic confirm a time or finish the booking. This is an abrupt, premature goodbye.

issues.quote: I'm sorry, I have to go now. I'll call back when I have my member ID. Thank you, goodbye.
issues.problem: After a long silence from the clinic, the bot abruptly says it has to go without first checking whether anyone is still on the line (e.g., 'Hello?'). It also leaves its pending questions about acceptance and the Sacramento address unresolved. This is an unnatural, premature hang-up.

issues.quote: I'm not sure which state the plan was issued in.
issues.problem: It is somewhat odd for a caller not to know which state their own new insurance plan was issued in.

issues.quote: Um, that sounds good, thank you. Just to confirm, you have my number as 650-996-3518, right? And is Dr. Okonkwo at your main office?
issues.problem: The bot asked the clinic to check the following week, but accepts a callback without noting that this was never done. It also asks whether Dr. Okonkwo is at the main office even though no time with him was offered, which sounds out of place.

issues.quote: who would you recommend for knee pain? Any of Dr. Hauser, Dr. Roth, or Dr. Bricker would be fine.
issues.problem: The bot asks for a recommendation and then immediately says any of them would be fine. This makes the question pointless and sounds slightly incoherent.

issues.quote: Um, that number isn't right. My number is 650-996-3518. And if Dr. Okonkwo isn't there, I'd be fine seeing Dr. Hauser, Dr. Roth, or
issues.problem: The bot repeats its previous turn almost word for word with no new clinic input in between. It also keeps talking after the call has ended.

issues.quote: It's for my upcoming appointment with Dr. Lukowski, so I just need a follow-up slot on Friday.
issues.problem: This is illogical: a follow-up visit would come after a past appointment, not an upcoming one. The doctor's name also appears out of nowhere.

issues.quote: They have a 1 PM slot on Friday, the 16th?
issues.problem: The caller refers to the clinic as 'they' while speaking directly to the clinic, which sounds like narration rather than conversation.

issues.quote: Friday the 17th doesn't work, then. My other option was November 31st, but that date doesn't exist, so I'm not sure what to do there.
issues.problem: The caller reads out the scripted fallback and then says it isn't a real date, which sounds like reciting instructions. It also says 'Friday the 17th' right after the clinic said the 17th is a Saturday, and never addresses that mismatch.

issues.quote: is there anything on Saturday, October nineteenth?
issues.problem: If Sunday is October 18th, that Saturday would be the 17th, not the 19th. The bot gets the date wrong.

issues.quote: Let's go with the ten thirty slot on Tuesday, October twentieth, then. Actually, I already have an appointment that day at 10 AM with Dr. Doogie Howser
issues.problem: The bot invents an existing appointment that contradicts its earlier framing of this as a new concern. It also accepts a weekday morning slot right after saying weekends are the only time it's free.

issues.quote: Hmm, that's different from what I have on file, which is 10 AM with Dr. Doogie Howser. Could you tell me what you have listed for the location and the time? Yes, a text confirmation would be great
issues.problem: The bot keeps pushing the invented prior appointment and mixes it awkwardly with accepting a text in the same turn.

issues.quote: Yes, that number is correct, please send the text confirmation. Thanks so much for your help, and goodbye!
issues.problem: This repeats the confirmation it already gave in the previous turn and arrives after the call had already ended.

issues.quote: Wait, you said Doogie Howser just now, but earlier you said Doogie Hauser. Which doctor is it?
issues.problem: Howser and Hauser sound the same when spoken, so a real caller couldn't hear a difference. The bot is reacting to speech-to-text spelling, not to what was actually said.

issues.quote: so I'll take the 9 AM if you can confirm the closing time.
issues.problem: Making the Thanksgiving booking depend on knowing the weekday closing time doesn't make sense. The two are unrelated, and the clinic had offered 8 AM first.

issues.quote: The provider keeps changing, and I still don't have a closing time. Can you
issues.problem: The bot keeps going back to the closing time and the provider name after the clinic has said twice that it doesn't have the closing time. It loops instead of finishing the booking.

issues.quote: That's right, though I think the doctor's name is Dr. Doogie Howser. I'd like a follow-up next week, ideally Tuesday morning if you have something open.
issues.problem: The bot 'corrects' a doctor name that would sound identical when spoken (Hauser/Howser). It also restates its Tuesday-morning preference for the third time, even though the clinic had just confirmed the request.

issues.quote: This is a test line, and the call has ended. I'm hanging up now.
issues.problem: The bot narrates the system state ('This is a test line', 'the call has ended') like a script rather than a real caller. It also speaks after the call has already ended.

issues.quote: Yes, my number is 650-555-0143.
issues.problem: The clinic asked for the number 'on file with us.' The bot had already said it was a new patient, yet it gave a number as if it had a record. It only mentioned not being on file one turn later.

issues.quote: I only have one appointment I know of, on Tuesday, October twentieth at 10 AM, with Dr. Doogie Howser.
issues.problem: The bot adds a specific 10 AM time that neither the scenario nor the clinic provided. It also says it only knows of one appointment, yet it accepts the unknown Thursday follow-up without any curiosity.

issues.quote: Now I want to confirm my appointment: Tuesday, October 20th at 10 AM with Dr. Doogie Howser.
issues.problem: The bot invents an existing appointment with a fictional TV doctor. This contradicts its opening line that it was calling to plan a visit, and nothing in the scenario supports it.

issues.quote: I've got to go. I'll call back when I have more time. Bye.
issues.problem: The bot hangs up abruptly right after asking two questions, before the clinic could answer. It abandons its own questions about the address and parking, and never gets to the planned probes.
